# conventions: nats; one 4-component field; one planar face; per unit area a^2; a = 1; ma = 0; one row per primitive cubic orbit (p1 >= p2 >= p3 >= 0), the 48 images to be generated by the reader.

# measured half-width (column eta_hw_measured): levels(h,h/2): eta = eta1 + (eta1-eta0)/10; hw = |eta1-eta0|/4 + chain_err(1.5 cL recompute) + ref_err/(3|p|) + 1e-9; valid if the grid error decreases at least as h^2 between the levels (h^4 log h observed in all 34 tested generic orbits; exact [100] and [111] reproduced to 1e-9)

# delivered half-width (column eta_hw, the one to use): exact rows eta = exact value to 12 decimals, eta_hw = 1.0e-12; generic rows 1 x measured; family rows with 3 levels max(measured, 1*|d_last|, 4e-06); family rows with 2 levels max(measured, 0*|d_last|, 4e-06).

# family: p1 = p2 > p3 (canonical orbit), the [110]-[111] edge, [110] included, [111] excluded: the two fast sines are degenerate, their fully dimerized line psi = pi/2 is a second non-analytic locus the node subtraction does not treat, and the level-0 grid (23 points) has a grid line on it while levels 1 and 2 do not; level ratios -12.5 to +14.7 in all 16 tested members

# the half-widths are measured enclosures under the stated premises, not certified intervals; eta is printed to 12 decimals (an inward error of at most 5e-13, inside the 1e-9 term of the measured rule); eta_hw is rounded outward at its last printed digit (the .3e format).

# eta_lev_a, eta_lev_b: the 2 finest grid levels used (levels[-2], levels[-1]); d_last = eta_lev_b - eta_lev_a; ratio = (change between the 2 coarser levels)/(change between the 2 finer levels) where 3 levels exist; eta_exact: the exact value to 20 digits for the exact rows.
